items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: because I had started out listening to that music and it was so much a part of my consciousness — you know, Louis, Bix, those tunes.

ctx.x: Well they’re mostly part-time guys. Well see the thing was that I was able to find a niche. I mean this is kind of interesting because this is sort of where this thing developed in my career, which has been kind of a blessing and a curse. Because now my orientation, when I left college — I went to college with Michael Brecker and I mean the stuff he was listening to then, his listening habits were a little more advanced than mine, I would say when we were in school, when we were like 18 or 19. I’d say mine were a…

Shorter or Miles was doing. Just when these records came out he had them. He was like listening to them day and night. And so that was part of it. When I was in college I mean Freddie Hubbard was my idol. I loved Freddie Hubbard and I liked to play in that sort of way. Well when I’m in New York and now it’s like early 80s, I just decided that I wanted to play and I wanted to take any jobs I could and get as close to jazz work as possible. Well at that time I just found this niche working in traditional jazz,…
Which shows up on your recent records.
